title: Support strided and broadcast sources when restoring quantized optimizer states
body:
## Problem

Quantized optimizer-state `copy_` handlers assume a contiguous, already expanded floating-point source. A transposed or sliced moment tensor can fail at `view`, while row and scalar sources do not implement ordinary `Tensor.copy_` broadcasting. This prevents restoring moments from a native AdamW checkpoint whose parameter and moment tensors use noncontiguous layouts.

## Change

Reshape floating-point inputs when forming quantization blocks and expand them to the destination's logical shape before quantization. Apply the same copy contract to the 4-bit, 8-bit, and FP8 optimizer states. Contiguous same-shape inputs retain the view fast path; inputs that require layout conversion allocate a reshaped copy.

## Validation

Native CPU PyTorch 2.14.0 with normal repository test configuration:

- 27 new cases cover contiguous, transposed, strided-row, strided-column, offset, expanded, row-broadcast, and scalar-broadcast sources, plus native checkpoint restoration for all three AdamW state formats.
- Original source: 21 failures and 6 passes. Patched source: 56 tests pass, including all 27 new cases and 29 existing quantization, slicing, dtype, and optimizer smoke cases.
- Copy tests compare packed codes, scales, and dequantized values to the result of native dense `Tensor.copy_`, and verify that the source data and strides remain unchanged.
- Real native AdamW moments are serialized from transposed parameters, copied into low-bit states, and used for three further compiled optimizer steps. Parameters and moment values match the equivalent contiguous restore exactly.
- Ruff 0.11.6 checks and formatting pass.

Exact production head: `6eda0c4e1c4003d68de96bf79fb3f5ec4383846f`.
